questions.question: Define demand and state the law of demand, including the condition attached to it.
questions.expected_answer: Demand is the quantity of a good or service that consumers are willing and able to buy at each possible price during a given period. Law of demand: other things remaining the same (ceteris paribus), when the price of a good rises the quantity demanded falls, and when the price falls the quantity demanded rises (an inverse relationship).

questions.question: Using the schedule R20: 50, R16: 80, R12: 120, R8: 170, R4: 230 muffins per day, describe how to draw the demand curve and calculate total spending at R20 and R12.
questions.expected_answer: Put price (rand) on the vertical axis and quantity demanded per day on the horizontal axis with suitable scales; plot the five points, join them with a smooth downward-sloping line, label it D and give the graph a heading. Spending at R20 = 20 × 50 = R1 000; at R12 = 12 × 120 = R1 440.

questions.question: Distinguish between a change in quantity demanded and a change in demand, giving a cause of each.
questions.expected_answer: A change in quantity demanded is a movement along the demand curve caused only by a change in the good's own price (e.g. muffin price falls from R16 to R12, quantity rises from 80 to 120). A change in demand is a shift of the whole curve caused by another factor: income, prices of substitutes or complements, tastes, population, expectations or government policy (e.g. a new school opens: demand shifts right).
